case.title: Malicious Python loader on GitHub
case.boundary: Static evidence supports a malicious multi-stage loader assessment. The unavailable final stage prevents reliable malware-family naming, data-theft claims or operator attribution. Similar-code search results are leads, not a campaign count.

nodes.label: Deceptive GitHub repository
nodes.meaning: A repository advertised as a Discord utility supplied the original Python artefact. The repository name alone was not treated as proof of malware.

nodes.label: Fernet decrypt-and-exec layer
nodes.meaning: The script silently installed dependencies, decrypted an embedded blob with a hard-coded key and passed plaintext to exec().

nodes.label: Two decoded retrieval locations
nodes.meaning: Static decoding recovered two defanged remote locations used as fallback retrieval points. One was already reputation-flagged during collection.

nodes.label: Encoded remote responses
nodes.meaning: Both locations returned another encoded layer at collection time, but a complete final payload was not recovered.

nodes.label: Hidden staged execution chain
nodes.meaning: Combining the decrypt-and-exec layer with encoded fallback retrieval, hidden temporary-file creation and background launch reconstructs a multi-stage execution chain.

nodes.label: Similar-code discovery leads
nodes.meaning: Point-in-time GitHub searches found repeated Fernet constructions. Forks, demonstrations and unrelated code make these results leads rather than a defensible cluster.

nodes.label: Malicious multi-stage loader
nodes.meaning: Suppressed installation, in-memory execution, encoded infrastructure and hidden process launch support a high-confidence malicious-loader assessment.

nodes.label: Final payload and actor unknown
nodes.meaning: The final stage was unavailable. The evidence cannot name an infostealer family, enumerate stolen data, attribute an operator or equate code similarity with common authorship.
